**Finding submitted — deviation (ASSIGN), preferred-level redline.**

- **Responsive clause:** ¶9(h) (p0072) is the sole assignment provision; no change-of-control clause exists anywhere (searches for "change of control"/"control" and the Term & Termination provisions at p0016–p0018 confirm no CoC trigger).
- **Why it fails:** the no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out is mutual, so Kubient may transfer the Agreement to any affiliate or acquirer — including an AP competitor — without our consent. That conflicts with the fallback requirement that non-successor assignments be consent-gated and with the preferred Vendor-side restrictions.
- **Cure (one surgical replace):** the proviso is limited to AP (preserving our affiliate/M&A freedom verbatim), Kubient is barred from assigning to an AP competitor, and a change of control of AP is confirmed to give Kubient no termination right. The retained first sentence already supplies the mutual "consent … not to be unreasonably withheld" standard, so that element was mapped as already met rather than restated.
- The post-Initial-Term 90-day termination right in ¶4(a) is a convenience issue for T4C and was deliberately not flagged here.
